description:
A network operations analyst is investigating intermittent connectivity issues reported by users. A packet capture has already been taken. Your job is to use Wireshark's Expert Information feature to get an automated diagnostic overview of all detected anomalies in the capture.

Open the file /home/ga/Documents/captures/200722_tcp_anon.pcapng in Wireshark. Use the Expert Information analysis (accessible via Analyze > Expert Information) to identify all diagnostic entries.

Create a report file saved to ~/Documents/captures/expert_info_report.txt with the following structure:

=== Expert Information Analysis Report ===
File: 200722_tcp_anon.pcapng

--- Summary by Severity ---
Errors: <count>
Warnings: <count>
Notes: <count>
Chats: <count>
Total: <count>

--- Top 3 Most Frequent Messages ---
1. <message text> (count: <N>)
2. <message text> (count: <N>)
3. <message text> (count: <N>)

--- Unique Message Types ---
Total unique message types: <count>

All counts must be accurate based on the actual Expert Information analysis of the capture file. The 'Top 3 Most Frequent Messages' should list the three expert info message texts that appear most often in the capture, along with their occurrence counts. 'Unique message types' is the count of distinct message text strings in the expert info output.
